name: Flask send_file with request-derived path
attack_scenario: GET /download?path=../../../../etc/passwd (or an absolute /etc/passwd) makes send_file stream arbitrary files readable by the service user, source code, secrets, SSH keys.
negative_test_hint: request the download endpoint with path = "../../../../etc/passwd" and assert the response is a 404 or 403 and the file contents are never streamed

exemplar.explanation: Flask's send_file() does NO path containment, it opens whatever path it is given. Feeding it a request-derived value (directly, via an f-string, or via concatenation) lets ../ sequences or an absolute path escape the intended directory. The third pattern is scoped to the user-controlled request accessors (args/form/values/json/view_args), so send_file(get_report_path(request.user.id)) is NOT flagged. send_from_directory() is the safe counterpart: it applies werkzeug safe_join and 404s on any traversal outside the base folder.
